# KaelosUI (`kaelos-core`)

> Animated, accessible tab bars for React. Six motion variants share one
> headless, framework-agnostic TypeScript core: measured geometry, real spring
> physics, CSS-variable theming, zero animation dependencies.

This document is written for an LLM or coding agent that has been asked to add
KaelosUI to an existing project. Work through it in order. Everything you are
allowed to import, pass or override is listed here - do not invent component
names, props or CSS variables.

---

## 0. What ships

- **Plain TypeScript source.** No build output, no bundler config, no runtime
  dependency. The consumer's bundler compiles it.
- **One stylesheet**, `src/styles/tabs.css`, exposed as `kaelos-core/styles.css`.
  It defines only `.tb-*` classes inside `@layer components`, so the host app's
  own utilities and design tokens still win without specificity fights.
  Tailwind is **not** required.
- **Peer dependencies:** `react` and `react-dom` (`>= 18`). Nothing else.
- **Package exports:**

  | Specifier | Resolves to |
  | --- | --- |
  | `kaelos-core` | `src/index.ts` (all components, types and the headless core) |
  | `kaelos-core/styles.css` | `src/styles/tabs.css` |

---

## 1. Install

The package is **not on npm**. Use the form that matches the project.

```bash
# Straight from GitHub
npm install github:R3plic/kaelos-core

# From a local checkout or a sibling directory
npm install file:../kaelos-core

# Already vendored as a git submodule
npm install file:./src/components/kaelos-core
```

### If you do not install it at all (submodule + path alias)

Wire up **both** specifiers - a bare-match alias alone will not resolve
`kaelos-core/styles.css`:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { fileURLToPath, URL } from 'node:url'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

const core = (p: string) => fileURLToPath(new URL(`./src/components/kaelos-core/${p}`, import.meta.url))

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: {
    alias: [
      { find: '@kaelos/core/styles.css', replacement: core('src/styles/tabs.css') },
      { find: /^@kaelos\/core$/, replacement: core('src/index.ts') },
    ],
  },
})
```

```json
// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@kaelos/core": ["./src/components/kaelos-core/src/index.ts"],
      "@kaelos/core/styles.css": ["./src/components/kaelos-core/src/styles/tabs.css"]
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 2. Import the stylesheet exactly once - required

```ts
import 'kaelos-core/styles.css'   // or '@kaelos/core/styles.css' when aliased
```

Put it in the application entry (`main.tsx`, `app/layout.tsx`, `_app.tsx`) or in
the global stylesheet. Without it the bars render as unstyled text.

If Tailwind v4 is present, order the imports so the component layer comes after
Tailwind:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import 'kaelos-core/styles.css';
```

---

## 3. Render a bar

```tsx
import { WormUnderlineTabs, HomeIcon, SearchIcon, UserIcon } from 'kaelos-core'
import 'kaelos-core/styles.css'

const items = [
  { id: 'home', label: 'Home', icon: <HomeIcon /> },
  { id: 'search', label: 'Search', icon: <SearchIcon /> },
  { id: 'profile', label: 'Profile', icon: <UserIcon /> },
]

export function Nav() {
  return <WormUnderlineTabs items={items} defaultValue="search" ariaLabel="Main" />
}
```

---

## 4. Choose a variant

| Component | Renders | Needs per item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WormUnderlineTabs` | Visible text labels + spring underline | `label`; `icon` optional |
| `HoppingDotTabs` | Icon rail, dot hops between icons | `icon` (falls back to the label's first letter) |
| `SpotlightTabs` | Icon rail + pivoting light cone | `icon` (same fallback) |
| `RippleFillTabs` | Icon rail, ripple fills the tapped tab | `icon` (same fallback) |
| `JellyIconTabs` | Icon rail, tapped icon squashes | `icon` (same fallback) |
| `BadgePopTabs` | Icon rail + count badges | `icon`, and `badge` for counts |

`label` is always the accessible name, even when it is not painted. Do not drop
it: the icon rail variants use it for `aria-label` and for the letter fallback.

---

## 5. Props (identical on all six)

```ts
interface TabItemSpec {
  id: string                     // stable identity, used for value/defaultValue and ARIA ids
  label: string                  // accessible name
  icon?: ReactNode               // any node: SVG, emoji, avatar
  badge?: number | string        // consumed by BadgePopTabs
  disabled?: boolean
}

interface BaseTabBarProps {
  items: TabItemSpec[]
  value?: string                 // controlled active id
  defaultValue?: string          // uncontrolled initial id
  onChange?: (item: TabItemSpec, index: number) => void
  id?: string                    // prefix for ARIA tab/panel ids
  ariaLabel?: string             // 'Categories' on WormUnderlineTabs, 'Navigation' elsewhere
  disabled?: boolean
  loop?: boolean                 // wrap arrow keys at the ends
  activation?: 'automatic' | 'manual'   // manual = Enter/Space activates
  withPanels?: boolean           // wires aria-controls to <TabPanel>s
  className?: string             // tab strip
  tabClassName?: string
  activeTabClassName?: string
  labelClassName?: string
  iconClassName?: string
  indicatorClassName?: string
  style?: CSSProperties          // token overrides, see tabVars below
}
```

`WormUnderlineTabs` additionally accepts `showLabels?: boolean` (default `true`;
when `false` the label becomes screen-reader-only).

Use **either** `value` (controlled) **or** `defaultValue` (uncontrolled), not
both.

---

## 6. Panels

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TabPanel, SpotlightTabs } from 'kaelos-core'

const [tab, setTab] = useState('home')

<SpotlightTabs
  id="app-nav"
  items={items}
  value={tab}
  onChange={(item) => setTab(item.id)}
  withPanels
/>
<TabPanel tabsId="app-nav" value="home">…</TabPanel>
```

`TabPanel`'s `tabsId` must equal the tab bar's `id`, and `value` must equal a
`TabItemSpec.id`.

---

## 7. Theming

Every colour, size, radius and spring constant is a CSS custom property. Pass
them with the typed helper, which keeps `style` type-safe:

```tsx
import { tabVars } from 'kaelos-core'

<WormUnderlineTabs
  items={items}
  style={tabVars({
    '--tb-accent': '#fb7185',
    '--tb-bar-bg': '#f6ecdf',
    '--tb-bar-radius': '15px',
    '--tb-text': '#2a1c0e',
  })}
/>
```

Shared tokens: `--tb-bar-bg`, `--tb-bar-border`, `--tb-bar-radius`,
`--tb-bar-padding`, `--tb-bar-shadow`, `--tb-text`, `--tb-text-soft`,
`--tb-muted`, `--tb-focus`, `--tb-accent`, `--tb-accent-2`, `--tb-tab-height`,
`--tb-tab-size`, `--tb-tab-font-size`, `--tb-icon-size`, `--tb-ring-color`.

Variant tokens (prefix per variant): `--tb-worm-*`, `--tb-hop-*`, `--tb-spot-*`,
`--tb-ripple-*`, `--tb-jelly-*`, `--tb-badge-*`. Grep `src/styles/tabs.css` for
the exact names and defaults before overriding - every declaration has a
fallback, so an unknown token is silently ignored.

Override per instance with `tabVars({...})`, per subtree with a wrapper class,
or globally on `:root`.

---

## 8. Icons

Nine ready-made 24×24 stroke icons accept any SVG props (`className`, `size`
via CSS): `HomeIcon`, `SearchIcon`, `HeartIcon`, `UserIcon`, `BellIcon`,
`BookmarkIcon`, `CompassIcon`, `SparkIcon`, `GridIcon`. Any `ReactNode` works as
`icon`, so lucide/react-icons or an `<img>` are equally valid.

---

## 9. Framework notes

- **Vite / esbuild / Bun:** works with no extra config, TS is transpiled from
  `node_modules` by default.
- **Next.js:** add `transpilePackages: ['kaelos-core']` to `next.config.*`, and
  put each component that uses a bar behind `'use client'` (they use hooks,
  refs and layout effects).
- **Webpack / Rspack:** if your `babel-loader` rule excludes `node_modules`,
  widen it to include `kaelos-core`, otherwise the `.tsx` source is not
  compiled.
- **Plain CSS consumers:** nothing else to do. No PostCSS plugin, no Tailwind
  content globs, no runtime JS beyond React.

---

## 10. Gotchas - read before you debug

1. **Missing stylesheet import** is by far the most common failure. The markup
   is unstyled text and raw icons. Check step 2 first.
2. **Do not re-implement the motion.** The bars animate by writing CSS
   variables from one shared rAF loop. Overriding `transform`/`transition` on
   `.tb-*` internals breaks the engines.
3. **Reduced motion** is honoured automatically; do not add your own media
   query around it.
4. **Rendering is measured.** Bars read `getBoundingClientRect` on mount. If the
   bar is inside a `display:none` container at mount, it will not animate until
   it is re-mounted or the layout changes.
5. **One bar per `id`.** ARIA ids are derived from `id`; duplicates collide.
6. **Do not fork the CSS.** Override tokens; do not copy `tabs.css` into the app
   and edit it, or you lose upgradeability.

---

## 11. Verify your integration

- The stylesheet is imported exactly once and the bar has its pill/rail styling.
- Clicking and arrow-keying changes the active tab, and `onChange` fires.
- `Tab` moves focus into the bar, arrows move within it, `Enter`/`Space`
  activates under `activation="manual"`.
- The bar has `role="tablist"` with one `role="tab"` per item and exactly one
  `aria-selected="true"`.
- No console warning about refs, hydration or missing keys.
